sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the editor logic
sections.what: Brings in the model types and the edit type used by the calculations.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: WbsNode
sections.title: WBS node shape
sections.what: Defines one node in the WBS tree: its path, label, depth and the component ids below it.
sections.why: Likely reason: a flat shape the tree view can display.

sections.name: wbsSegments
sections.title: Splitting WBS paths
sections.what: Splits a WBS path into segments, accepting several separators, and also handles dotted numbers like 1.2.3.
sections.why: Likely reason: source files use different separators, so one parser handles them all.
sections.watch_out: A single dotted word is treated as segments, so an unusual name with a dot could split unexpectedly.

sections.name: canonicalWbs
sections.title: Canonical WBS text
sections.what: Joins the segments of a path back into one standard text form.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives every path one consistent spelling for comparison.

sections.name: matchesWbs
sections.title: Whole-segment path match
sections.what: Checks whether one path sits under another, comparing whole segments so that 20 never matches 2.
sections.why: Likely reason: prevents sibling branches from being wrongly included in a filter.
sections.watch_out: Both paths must split the same way, or the match can fail.

sections.name: componentWbsPaths
sections.title: Component path lookup
sections.what: Returns the WBS paths for each component, using its supplied paths first and the older structure group as a fallback.
sections.why: Likely reason: supports older data that has only a group name.
sections.watch_out: Components with no path at all are returned with an empty list, so they will not appear in the tree.

sections.name: buildWbsNodes
sections.title: Building the WBS tree
sections.what: Builds one tree node for each path level and records which components belong under it, sorted by path.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the tree show every branch with the right component counts.
sections.watch_out: A component on several branches appears in each one, so totals across the tree can count it more than once.

sections.name: nodesAtLevel, degreesToRadians, radiansToDegrees
sections.title: Level filtering and angle conversion
sections.what: Chooses the nodes to show at a given depth, keeping shorter leaves visible. Also converts between degrees and radians.
sections.why: Likely reason: shallow branches would otherwise vanish when a deeper level is chosen.
sections.watch_out: Conversion helpers return plain numbers, so the caller must keep the units straight.

sections.name: validateVector
sections.title: Vector check
sections.what: Confirms that x, y and z are finite numbers, and optionally that they are all positive.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops invalid geometry from being saved.

sections.name: assetSpecificationEdits
sections.title: Asset specification edits
sections.what: Calculates the saved changes for one asset. It scales the sibling phases in proportion, keeps their relative offsets, keeps the bottom height fixed, and applies the requested rotation as a difference.
sections.why: Likely reason: preserves each phase's shape instead of copying the selected one.
sections.watch_out: Dimension scaling and base height both affect results, so changing one must be checked against the height calculation.

sections.name: spacingEdits
sections.title: Spacing edits into a grid
sections.what: Places selected assets into rows and columns with the chosen gaps, moving every phase of each asset together, and limits the batch size.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets users arrange many assets evenly without moving each part by hand.
sections.watch_out: The batch limit of 2,048 edits is enforced, and a row size that is too small can produce a very tall grid.

summary: Holds the logic that the parametric model editor uses: reading and matching WBS paths, building the WBS tree, and calculating edits for asset resizing, moving and spacing.
purpose: Lets users edit a schedule-based model safely by computing the exact changes to save, without touching the originals.
why: Likely reason: keeping the calculations separate from the display makes them testable.
how: Splits WBS paths into segments and matches them by whole segment. It builds a tree of paths with their component ids. For specification edits, it computes scaled sizes and offsets for sibling phases relative to the selected one. For spacing, it places assets in a grid of rows and columns using their bounding boxes.
inputs: A project model, selected components, the user's edit request, and gap and column settings.
outputs: WBS paths and trees, true or false for vector checks, and lists of component edits to save, or an error message.
risks: Asset batches are limited to 2,048 phase edits. Cylinder parts need equal X and Z scaling. Mistakes in offset calculations would move equipment incorrectly, so the tests matter.
debug: If an edit lands in the wrong place, check the sibling offset calculation and the base height. If spacing looks wrong, check the bounding box calculation. If an error appears, read its message, since each one names the rule it broke.
